Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked quote shortest decisive line. 1: # Workstreams — how to split the work across agents
2: 
3: Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
4: builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
5: and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
6: until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.
7: 
8: ## Starting an agent
9: 
10: Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
11: work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
12: ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
13: and "done when".
14: 
15: ## UI agents (WS2–WS4)
16: 
17: The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
18: `api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
19: `not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
20: controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
21: screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
22: `apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.
23: 
24: ## Git
25: 
26: Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
27: commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
28: with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
29: `package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.
30: 
31: ## Phases
32: 
33: 0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
34:    contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
35:    Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
36: 1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
37: 2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
38:    to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.

43: 
44: **Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.

46: integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.

58:   inner workplaces via boundary blocks, merge per input port, per-port output storage, failure →

100: `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/globals.css`, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml`, `apps/desktop/build/**` (app icons).
101: **State today:** bottom tab bar (⌘/Ctrl 1–3), Settings with App, Global parameters, AI & research,
102: Collaboration and About; theme switching (system/light/dark); every change validated with the
103: `Settings` schema. Not saved yet (waits for WS1's `settings.save`).
104: **Builds next:** API-key entry once `settings.setSecret` exists (never display a stored key), a
105: `settings.changed` audit entry once WS1 logs it, the app icon and installer config, demo polish.
106: **Done when:** settings load, validate, save and appear as a `settings.changed` audit event, the shell looks
107: demo-ready, and `npm run package` produces a working installer on your OS.
108: 
109: ### WS5 — Raw block (BMW data ingestion)
110: 
111: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/raw/**`, `data/samples/**`.
112: **Builds:** the Raw block. Params (see `BLOCK_SPECS.raw`): Excel upload (`file` = `{ fileId, name }`
113: from `api.files.import()`, `sheet`) or database (`dbType`, `connection`, `query`; never store
114: passwords in params), plus `dataset`. It parses the provided formats (CSV, XLSX and whatever BMW
115: ships: check `data/raw/` once it arrives) into `Source` + `SourceRecord[]` with locators and language.
116: Structured datasets (equipment take rates, sales volumes) also emit deterministic `usage_pattern`
117: findings (for example a high take rate signals a basic expectation) with evidence. Also write
118: synthetic sample files in `data/samples/` that match the real formats. Param changes → request via WS0.
119: **Done when:** each sample dataset ingests in tests, errors name the bad row or column, and no data is dropped silently.
120: 
121: ### WS6 — Research block
122: 
123: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/research/**`.
124: **Builds:** the Research block. It turns its params and the scope into queries (competitors in the
125: segment, owner and press reviews, market and technology trends for the horizon), runs them through
126: `ctx.web`, fetches pages and extracts clean text into `SourceRecord`s — the same stream format as Raw —
127: and sets the `Source` kind, publisher, date and **reliability** (with the rule documented). It respects
128: allowed and blocked domains and de-duplicates by URL. Also implement `WebSearch` providers
129: (`anthropic_web_search`, `tavily`) as factories that take keys as arguments (WS1 wires them).
130: **Done when:** a recorded or offline test run produces sources with working URLs and reliability, and failures are logged rather than swallowed.
131: 
132: ### WS7 — AI blocks: AI Filter, AI Splitter, Add to Car
133: 
134: **Owns:** `packages/llm/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-splitter/**`,
135: `packages/blocks/src/add-to-car/**`.
136: **Builds:** an `LlmClient` with a Claude provider and a deterministic `mock` provider (use the `claude-api`
137: skill for SDK details). **AI Filter**: keep items matching the criterion and extract evidence-linked
138: findings (verbatim-excerpt verification; out-of-scope items logged with a reason). **AI Splitter**:
139: route every item to exactly one branch (`out-<i>`); "Split by: Priority" uses WS8's scoring.
140: **Add to Car**: cluster and derive customer-facing, actionable requirements (IDs from
141: `formatRequirementId`, measurable targets, evidence level per the A–D rule, Kano class, assumptions,
142: uncertainties, conflicting findings), set the priority from the input port's ranking, and hand them
143: to `ctx.car.add`. Also export `answerChallenge(...)` for the API's challenge flow.
144: **Done when:** fixture records → filter → splitter → Add to Car runs fully offline with `mock`, all
145: outputs parse against the core schemas, and every finding's excerpt is verified.

149: **Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/prioritization/**`.

151: deterministically where possible: customer impact from mentions, sentiment and sales volume; evidence

153: `competitor_advantage` findings; trend momentum from `market_trend` findings. The LLM is used only

155: and `priorityForScore` and writes a readable `priorityRationale` naming the top drivers. It also flags
156: "high score, weak evidence".
157: **Done when:** scores are reproducible for the fixtures, changing Settings weights changes the ranking as
158: expected (tested), and each factor has a note a PM can understand.

479: async function execute(

481:   input: Record<string, unknown>,

483:   ctx: ProviderContext,
484:   signal: AbortSignal,

521:     signal.throwIfAborted();
522:     startAttempted = true;
523:     const started = await json(

525:       "POST",
526:       input,
527:     );
528:     // Retain a safe run ID even when the rest of the response is malformed, so cleanup remains possible.
529:     const identity = z.object({ data: z.object({ id: Identifier }) }).safeParse(started);
530:     if (identity.success) runId = identity.data.data.id;
531:     let run = Run.parse(started).data;
532:     terminal = TERMINAL.has(run.status);
533:     while (!terminal) {
534:       signal.throwIfAborted();
535:       const wait = Math.max(1, Math.min(5, Math.floor((deadline - Date.now()) / 1000)));
536:       run = Run.parse(await json(`/actor-runs/${runId}?waitForFinish=${wait}`)).data;
537:       if (run.id !== runId) throw new Error("malformed run identity");
538:       terminal = TERMINAL.has(run.status);
539:     }
540:     signal.throwIfAborted();
541:     if (run.status !== "SUCCEEDED")
542:       note(
543:         `${actor} ended with ${run.status}; existing dataset records are retained when available.`,
544:       );

546:     let offset = 0;
547:     while (offset < rowLimit) {
548:       const limit = Math.min(50, rowLimit - offset);
549:       const parameters = new URLSearchParams({
550:         format: "json",
551:         clean: "false",
552:         offset: String(offset),
553:         limit: String(limit),
554:       });
555:       const page = await json(`/datasets/${run.defaultDatasetId}/items?${parameters}`);
556:       if (!Array.isArray(page)) throw new Error("malformed dataset envelope");
557:       signal.throwIfAborted();
558:       if (page.length > limit)
559:         note(
560:           `${actor} returned more dataset items than requested; excess records were not collected.`,
561:         );
562:       for (const value of page.slice(0, limit)) {
563:         if (done()) break;
564:         row(value);
565:       }
566:       offset += Math.min(page.length, limit);
567:       if (page.length < limit || done()) break;
568:     }
569:   } catch (error) {
570:     if (
571:       startAttempted &&
572:       !runId &&
573:       !(
574:         error instanceof ProviderError &&
575:         ["invalid_credentials", "permission_required", "limit_reached"].includes(error.code)
576:       )
577:     ) {
578:       note(
579:         "Actor start was not confirmed and its run ID is unknown; abort is impossible. Costs may continue until the server timeout.",
580:       );
581:     }
582:     throw error;
583:   } finally {
584:     if (runId && !terminal) {
585:       // The cancelled collection signal must not cancel its cleanup. Still use the common HTTP service.
586:       const cleanup = new AbortController();
587:       const timer = setTimeout(() => cleanup.abort(), 5000);
588:       try {
589:         const response = Run.parse(
590:           await ctx.http.json(`${API}/actor-runs/${runId}/abort?gracefully=false`, {
591:             method: "POST",
592:             headers: headers(token),
593:             signal: cleanup.signal,
594:           }),
595:         ).data;
596:         if (response.id !== runId || response.status !== "ABORTED") {
597:           note(
598:             "Actor abort was requested but final termination is not confirmed; costs may continue until termination or the server timeout.",
599:           );
600:         } else {
601:           note(
602:             "Actor was aborted; costs already incurred and costs during cancellation are not refunded.",
603:           );
604:         }
605:       } catch {
606:         note(
607:           "Actor abort is not confirmed; costs may continue until the server timeout. Check the Apify console.",
608:         );
609:       } finally {
610:         clearTimeout(timer);
611:       }
612:     }
613:   }

+
+`packages/blocks/src/research/http.ts` is the main-process transport boundary for

+export interface RequestBudget {
+  used: number;
+}
+
+export interface ProviderHttpOptions {
+  limits: ResearchLimits;
+  signal: AbortSignal;
+  fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;

+export function createProviderHttp(
+  options: ProviderHttpOptions,
+): ProviderHttpClient;

+and pass that exact object to `createProviderHttp`. Before each external planner
+call, check `budget.used < limits.maxRequests` and increment `budget.used`
+synchronously, with no intervening `await`. Every ordinary HTTP attempt performs
+the same check and reservation. Retries and failed attempts consume the budget.
+Separate HTTP clients can share this object, although their concurrency and
+provider-credit limits remain local to each client. Prefer one HTTP client per
+run for a shared concurrency and credit limit.
+
+`http.requests` counts **HTTP attempts only**, including actor cleanup. It never
+counts planner calls, cache hits, queued requests cancelled before dispatch, or
+requests rejected before dispatch. `http.cleanupRequests` is the cleanup subset.
+The shared `budget.used` includes planner and ordinary HTTP attempts but excludes
+the explicitly reserved cleanup allowance. Consequently, `http.requests` can
+exceed `limits.maxRequests` by at most four reserved cleanup attempts. Report
+cleanup as an additional allowance rather than claiming that `maxRequests` is
+an absolute limit on all network traffic. A total external-attempt report can
+use `budget.used + http.cleanupRequests`; a transport-only report uses
+`http.requests`.

+## Endpoint and failure policy
+
+Only HTTPS requests to the explicit provider hosts are accepted: Firecrawl,
+Tavily, Google/YouTube, Apify, X/Twitter, Reddit, OpenAlex, and the Eurostat host.
+URL credentials, explicit ports (including `:443`), alternate hosts, IP literals,
+and malformed URLs are rejected before transport. Fetch uses `redirect: "error"`
+and never follows a provider redirect to another endpoint.
+
+Authentication headers are redacted before generic key/value fields, so
+`Authorization: Bearer ...` and `Authorization: Basic ...` cannot leave the token
+behind. Explicit secret values are also removed in raw, percent-encoded, and
+form-encoded representations. Percent escape casing does not affect redaction;
+the case of literal secret characters remains significant.
+
+Network exceptions, response-stream exceptions, malformed JSON, and body cleanup
+exceptions never retain transport messages or response content. HTTP failures
+retain only the status and a fixed `ProviderError` message. Responses are limited
+to 16 MiB, both by declared content length and by actual streamed bytes. Unicode
+is decoded after byte collection, preserving characters split across chunks.

+## Concurrency, cancellation, and retries
+
+One FIFO semaphore holds each slot through response-body consumption. Release
+transfers the occupied slot directly to the next waiter, so new callers cannot
+steal a queued caller's slot or increase the configured upper bound. A queued
+request listens to its own combined run/request signal; cancellation removes it
+from the queue immediately without consuming a transport attempt or leaking a
+slot.

+uncooperative stream cleanup must not keep the caller pending. This guarantees
+local settlement, not physical termination of a noncooperative transport or
+remote work. Retry timers and abort listeners are removed on both completion and
+cancellation.
